Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The PR changes posted G-code.

The cumulative A count, travel refusal, and section-end G94 tests pass. The decision record identifies the Hub readings and the remaining hardware checks.

Local results against upstream/main `4e8616b81a43795a8587fa70e84045fb4065c190`:

- The trial merge is clean. The PR already contains this main commit.
- The selected camcraft-app and camcraft-post test targets build.
- Eleven selected suites pass: first_4axis_part (4), fourth_axis_pose (9), index_swing (13), recorded_post_streams (5), rotary_feed_cap (11), tormach_fourth_axis (12), tormach_post (10), tormach_wrapped_a (10), explain_tormach (3), recorded_streams (12), and script_tormach (11).
- microarc_test_part: 1 passes; 1 fails.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- The site test file has 11 passes and 1 known failure. `test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones` searches posting.rs for the machine name. That source is unchanged from main. This is not a new blocker.
- The quick dry run selects 588 steps because the golden is shared input. I ran the affected suites listed above.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Bound the actual part-relative path when you calculate feed time.** `assets/posts/tormach.cps:875` uses the distance between the stream endpoints. During a turning move, the actual path between those endpoints is curved. The rounding allowance does not bound that extra length. I reproduced this with a rapid to world `(0, 0, 10)` at A0, followed by a feed to the same world point at A3 and F0.1 mm/min. The unmodified post reports no warning and writes:

   ```text
   G93 G1 X0 Y0.523 Z9.986 A3 F57.735
   ```

   I sampled the posted XYZ/A interpolation at 10,000 intervals and transformed each point back into the part frame. The path is 0.006861819 mm long. Its average feed is 0.396167 mm/min, almost four times the requested feed. The bow passes the existing split check. Calculate a conservative bound from the posted trajectory, including rounding, or refuse this case. Add an independent test that checks the interpolated trajectory and the feed limit.

2. **[P2] Make the new golden test pass across supported platforms.** `crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs:265` fails on Linux. Both programs have 3,245 lines, but nine lines differ. For example, golden line 265 has `A-42.717`; Linux emits `A-42.718`. Lines 1040-1041 change `A-41.921 F116.959` / `A-45 F116.921` to `A-41.922 F116.921` / `A-45 F116.959`. The other differences are at lines 1124-1125, 2477-2478, and 2939-2940. Use deterministic output rounding or a narrowly bounded numeric comparison. Keep the independent A-rate and feed checks. Replacing the golden with one platform's output alone does not establish a cross-platform fix.

   ```text
   a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a ... FAILED
   wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc is stale; regenerate with WRITE_GOLDEN=1
   test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed
   ```

Mutation checks:

- I applied two mutations to the CPS text in memory through a temporary harness outside the repository.
- Remove the A-rate time bound: the rotary-rate test fails. It emits F598.962 instead of F4.
- Remove angle unwrapping: the cumulative-A test fails. It emits A-179 instead of A181.
- With both mutations absent, all 10 original wrapped-A tests pass again.
- The separate trajectory/feed test fails on the unmodified post with the values in finding 1.

Golden checks: I checked every NC line for positive feed words, A travel, turning-feed mode, A rate, and G94 at M5. These checks pass for both programs. They do not cover finding 1. The changed tilt refusal matches the recorded-stream tests.

Notes: No UI code changes. No build script, workflow, script, or dependency changes. No GitHub runner was used. No repository code or golden was changed. The exact posted program and a hardware cut remain untested, as the PR body states. Issue #796 still lists a hardware cut as an acceptance condition.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Full quick gate (M5, dude, head `ef864e37d` trial-merged with upstream/main `7903db4dc`): **587 of 588 steps pass**. The one failure is this PR's own new golden: `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` - `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc is stale` against current main, so a toolpath change that reached main after this branch was cut moves the wrapped program. On the next refresh (`git merge upstream/main`), regenerate it with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` and read the golden diff line by line before committing: it is posted G-code. Note also #2343 (found while writing #2346): Rotary Parallel finishes the model's end faces down to the axis, which this golden shares - simulator and air cut only until that is settled.

Addressed:

- P1: Feed time now uses a conservative bound on the rounded posted XYZ/A trajectory in the part frame. `posted_trajectory_length_obeys_the_feed_even_for_coincident_world_endpoints` independently samples 10,000 intervals per move in metric and inch cases. The old post fails the pin at 0.396167 mm/min for F0.1. The restored fix passes all 11 wrapped-A tests.
- P2: The wrapped golden comparison permits at most 0.001 degree of A rounding on G0/G1 and 0.04 inverse minutes of F rounding on G93 turning feeds. Other words stay exact. `wrap_golden_allows_only_bounded_platform_rounding` pins the reported rapid and feed differences and rejects larger differences or changed motion words. Exact-comparison mutation fails; restoration passes. All three microARC tests pass. The golden was refreshed for the corrected trajectory bound. Independent feed and A-rate checks remain.

Validation: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 588 steps. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

Please re-review this head.

  FAIL: test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones

The quick dry run selects 624 steps on the trial merge, including unrelated suites. I ran the affected suites listed above.

Requested before merge:

1. **Correct the simulator test claim.** `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-4axis-part.md:33` says continuous output has run in the PathPilot simulator. Lines 379–380 repeat this claim. The PR body states that this program has not run there. Issue #796 records four hand-written motion tests, not a posted continuous program. State that those tests confirm the control behavior. State separately that the posted continuous program still needs a simulator run and a hardware check. Update the site test that requires the current wording.

2. **Make the G93 guide consistent.** `site/content/guide/multi-axis/continuous-4-axis.md:45` adds Tormach G93 support. But lines 35–41 still say no shipped post supports inverse time. Line 78 still lists inverse-time feed as unimplemented. Update both sections to describe the Tormach exception and the limits of the other posts. The current instructions give opposite answers about the same feature.

Safety checks:

- I repeated the old-chord mutation in an external harness. The new trajectory test fails at the earlier case: 0.396167 mm/min for a requested 0.1 mm/min. With the trajectory bound restored, the test passes in metric and inch units.
- I removed the A-rate time bound in memory. The rate test fails: F598.962 replaces F4. With the bound restored, it passes.
- I repeated the exact-comparison mutation. The platform-rounding test fails. With the bounded comparator restored, it passes.
- All 11 wrapped-A tests pass with no mutation. These checks changed no repository file.
- I checked all 3,245 NC lines and all 529 changed lines since the earlier reviewed head. Changes affect A and F words only. XYZ words and motion structure stay unchanged.
- The independent trajectory audit finds a maximum feed of 203.17537 mm/min, below 203.2 mm/min. The maximum A rate is 360 deg/min. Feed modes, positive feeds, A travel, and G94 at section ends pass.
- The changed recorded refusal correctly identifies the unsupported B30 tilt.

Notes: The PR changes no UI code, build script, workflow, script, or dependency. No GitHub runner was used. No code or golden was changed. The posted program and a hardware cut remain untested. Issue #796 still includes a hardware cut in its acceptance condition.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

- Corrected the G93 guide's feed and unimplemented sections. They now describe Tormach's simultaneous A-about-X exception and the limits of other posts. `test_continuous_feed_guide_states_the_tormach_exception_consistently` pins both sections.

<!-- review-cost: effort:high · escalated: no -->
**Verdict: needs-rework. Built locally on Windows at this head.** The suite is red on the exact test the prior blocker named. The PR's claim that all tests pass with the bounded comparator does not hold here.

**Finding 1 (blocker): the golden comparator is red on Windows.** `microarc_test_part` fails: `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, line 661: `F209.668 != F209.79` (allowance 0.04). Regenerating the golden on this machine with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` changes 11 of 3245 lines. All A deltas are exactly 0.001 deg (inside the allowance at crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs:276-277). The F deltas are 0.049, 0.122, 0.414 and 0.749 - up to 19 times the 0.04 allowance at :278-279. Root cause: the split loop in assets/posts/tormach.cps:872 (`while (n < TURN_MAX && !(turnBow(s, e, a0, a1, n) <= TURN_TOL)) n *= 2;`). One 1-ULP libm difference flips the split-boundary decision, and a flipped split changes whole adjacent F words, not the last place. The structure is not in question: line count, word count, XYZ words and modes are byte-identical between the goldens; only A and F words differ. The A allowance is harmless (0.001 deg is about 0.17 um of tip travel at the 9.525 mm radius, far under TURN_TOL = 0.005 mm at tormach.cps:792). The F allowance is mis-shaped: an absolute 0.04 is smaller than the real platform spread, and an absolute of 0.75 or more would hide a 14 percent speed error on the lowest-F turning line (F5.335). The fix must remove the platform dependence (a margin or quantization in the bow test), or bound the delta relative to the F value. A PR never changes a golden by hand; a release-lane refresh is not the route either - the machine-to-machine spread must go from the post or the comparator first.

**Finding 2 (open, latent): a turning rapid does not restate G94.** `motionFor` restates G94 only when `!aNext` (tormach.cps:800-801), and the turning-rapid branch writes no restatement (tormach.cps:890-891): `if (rapid) { block(["G0", xw, yw, zw, aw]); }`. A turning rapid directly after a turning G93 feed posts G0 in G93 mode. This contradicts the decision doc (docs/decisions/796-tormach-wrapped-a.md:33-35: cycles, arcs, probes and the next operation "never run in G93"). The shipped golden does not exercise it (0 of 195 turning rapids in G93) and no test pins it. Add the restatement or a refusal, plus a test.

**Finding 3 (cosmetic):** tormach.cps:725 sets `aNext = { a: to, word: tw };` - the `word` field is never read; only `aNext.a` is (tormach.cps:870).

**What is correct here.** The feed law holds: `turnLength` (tormach.cps:848-860) is a valid arc-length bound, `t = max((length + slack) / f, dA / rate)` at :898 with the A rate 360 deg/min from assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch:30, and the overflow paths refuse by name (:900-902). The dense-sampling test in crates/app/tests/tormach_wrapped_a.rs pins tip speed at or under feed independently of the golden. On the golden the maximum A rate is 360.0000000000003 deg/min - no violation.

**Gate (Windows debug, worktree at f29c92bd1):** microarc_test_part 2 passed 1 FAILED; tormach_wrapped_a 11; rotary_feed_cap 11; recorded_post_streams 5; tormach_post 10; conformance 7; posting 17; post crate: script_tormach 7, g93_feed 3, cycle_hop 5, recorded_streams 12, explain_tormach 11; clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings clean.

**Label note.** This PR carries `merge-ready` set from the author's own review. That does not count under "Only collaborators' reviews count" (AGENTS.md): the review must be by an agent that did not write the change. This review is not clean, so the label goes to `needs-rework` and the PR goes back to draft.
